nodes.summary: The qpGraph design matrix of basis statistics `f4 (A i) (B i) (C i) (D i)` for lineage weights `w`: entry `(i, e)` is `(w Aᵢ e - w Bᵢ e) * (w Cᵢ e - w Dᵢ e)`.
nodes.title: qpGraph design matrix of basis f4 statistics

nodes.summary: Uniqueness of the GLS maximizer: for positive definite `Q` and a design matrix of full column rank (`B.mulVec` injective), a vector `ℓ` with the same score as a solution `ℓ̂` of the normal equations equals `ℓ̂`.
nodes.title: Uniqueness of the generalized least-squares maximizer

nodes.summary: `S2` is not basis independent (Patterson et al. 2012, after eq. 7): there are a positive definite covariance `Q`, an invertible change of basis `A` and statistics `f`, `g` such that, for every `λ`, the score changes.
nodes.title: The qpGraph score S2 depends on the basis

nodes.summary: In the drift model, with the admixture weights fixed, the predicted statistics are linear in the edge lengths: `g = B ℓ` for the design matrix `B`.
nodes.title: Predicted f4 statistics are linear in the edge lengths

nodes.summary: For positive definite `Q` and a design matrix of full column rank, the GLS Gram matrix `Bᵀ Q⁻¹ B` is invertible.
nodes.title: Invertibility of the generalized least-squares Gram matrix

nodes.summary: The closed-form GLS estimate `ℓ̂ = (Bᵀ Q⁻¹ B)⁻¹ Bᵀ Q⁻¹ f` solves the normal equations when the Gram matrix is invertible.
nodes.title: Closed-form generalized least-squares estimate of edge lengths

nodes.summary: `S1` is basis independent: under an invertible change of basis `A` of the statistics, with the covariance transformed to `A Q Aᵀ`, the score is unchanged. (The identity holds for every `Q`; for singular `Q` both sides are `0` by Mathlib's convention `Q⁻¹ = 0`.)
nodes.title: Basis independence of the qpGraph score S1

nodes.summary: GLS maximizes `S1`: for positive definite `Q`, a solution `ℓ̂` of the normal equations `Bᵀ Q⁻¹ B ℓ̂ = Bᵀ Q⁻¹ f` maximizes `ℓ ↦ S1(B ℓ)` over all `ℓ`.
nodes.title: Solutions of the normal equations maximize the score S1

nodes.summary: The qpGraph score `S1(g) = -½ (g - f)ᵀ Q⁻¹ (g - f)` (Patterson et al. 2012, eq. 6) of predicted statistics `g` against estimated statistics `f` with error covariance `Q`.
nodes.title: Generalized least-squares qpGraph score S1

nodes.summary: `S2` is twice `S1` with the covariance replaced by the diagonal matrix of the `Qᵢᵢ + λ`, when these are nonzero.
nodes.title: Score S2 as score S1 with a diagonal covariance

nodes.summary: The least-squares qpGraph score `S2(g) = -∑ᵢ (gᵢ - fᵢ)² / (Qᵢᵢ + λ)` (Patterson et al. 2012, eq. 7). A term with `Qᵢᵢ + λ = 0` is `0` by the convention `x / 0 = 0`.
nodes.title: Least-squares qpGraph score S2
